title: The Many Critics of JD Vance
author: Julia Yost
content:
![The Many Critics of JD
Vance](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/08/55238094407_135ba864b7.jpg)

> _Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith_  
>  By JD Vance  
> Harper, 295 pages, $35

In 2016, JD Vance's _Hillbilly Elegy_ , a memoir of ascent from Appalachia to
Yale Law, became the definitive professional-class explainer on Trumpism. This
summer, Vance's follow-up memoir has him finding his way from Yale back to
religious faith and a few other middle-American things, such as distrust of
elite prescriptions for personal and societal flourishing. An apologia for his
conversions to both Catholicism and Trumpism, _Communion_ has had strong sales
and a rough reception outside of pro-Trump outlets. The book narrates changes
of mind and heart, and provides grounds for reasonable criticism of its author
and his transformations. Unfortunately, its mainstream reviewers haven't found
them.

> "They loved _Hillbilly Elegy_."

_Communion_ is [_disparaged_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/20/opinion/jd-
vance-communion-trump.html?ref=compactmag.com) as a mishmash of genres:
conversion memoir, policy defense of Trump II, groundlaying for 2028.
Reviewers' complaints about the book's formal incoherence reflect a
substantive judgment against Vance's professional, ideological, and spiritual
transits. They loved _Hillbilly Elegy_ for the way it blamed downscale whites
for their problems. _Communion_ , by trashing the professional-class community
quartered at Yale and in Silicon Valley, reminds them why they went from
feting Vance to hating him. You don't come up from Middletown, achieve
professional-class nirvana, and then decide that Mamaw was right after all. So
reviewers find ways of saying (as Tim Walz did during the 2024 campaign) that
Vance is "creepy and, yes, just weird as hell."

Attacking--sorry, advocating for--the wife is a favorite tactic. Usha
Chilukuri Vance is the book's second leading character, who despite being a
secular Hindu helped to restore JD's faith in Christianity. Concerned
feminists seem to regard Usha's role in her husband's redemption as beneath
her, or constraining, or something. _The Cut_
[_headlines_](https://www.thecut.com/article/jd-vance-communion-book-review-
catholicism.html?ref=compactmag.com), "JD Vance Wrote a Book To Convince You
His Wife Doesn't Hate Him." The reviewer, Ginny Hogan, is incredulous that
Usha, the former star of Yale Law and clerk for Chief Justice John Roberts,
could approve of JD's conversion to Catholicism or actually want this fourth
child they had in July. No woman ascends to corporate-law officemaxxing and
then embraces a conservative vision of motherhood. Something weird is going
on.
